title: ALT5 Sigma $1.5B WLFI treasury deal
summary: WLF and Nasdaq-listed ALT5 Sigma did announce a $1.5B WLFI-treasury deal on Aug 11, 2025. Reporting does say about $500M went to a Trump-family entity (DT Marks DEFI LLC) and about $90M to the Witkoffs, but these are journalists' estimates from the 75% token-sale-proceeds entitlement, not audited payment records. ALT5's stock lost roughly 90-96% from its pre-deal price, and the company renamed itself AI Financial Corporation (AIFC) in April 2026. The weakest part is 'run by the same people': WLF insiders control ALT5's board, starting with chairman Zach Witkoff, but its CEOs have come from outside WLF.

sub_claims.statement: World Liberty announced a $1.5 billion deal with ALT5 Sigma.
sub_claims.finding: Announced Aug 11, 2025: 200M ALT5 shares at $7.50 in a registered direct offering plus a concurrent private placement, with WLF as lead investor. About $750M was paid in WLFI tokens (priced at $0.20) and about $750M in cash from outside investors, which went mostly to buying WLFI from WLF. Strictly, the $1.5B was ALT5's raise with WLF as lead investor. It was not WLF itself 'going to the stock markets'.

sub_claims.statement: The deal reportedly made $500 million for a Trump family-owned entity.
sub_claims.finding: The WSJ (Aug 31, 2025) said the deal 'stands to earn over half a billion dollars' for the Trump family. CNBC (June 9, 2026) said company disclosures show the family was 'entitled to roughly $500 million'. The entity is DT Marks DEFI LLC, which under WLF's token-offering documents gets 75% of net token-sale proceeds. The figure is an estimate after fees; no filing shows the actual amount paid. 'Reportedly' is the right qualifier.

sub_claims.statement: The deal reportedly made $90 million for the Witkoff family.
sub_claims.finding: Coverage of a Feb 2026 WSJ feature (via crypto.news and Benzinga) says 'more than $500 million flowed to Trump entities and $90 million to Witkoffs through this structure'. I could not read the WSJ text myself, so this rests on secondary reporting. Separately, the same WSJ reporting puts total Witkoff earnings from WLF at $200M or more.

sub_claims.statement: ALT5 Sigma is run by the same people who run World Liberty Financial.
sub_claims.finding: There is real overlap at board level. WLF CEO Zach Witkoff became ALT5's chairman, Eric Trump was announced as a director, and WLF co-founder Zak Folkman later joined as a director (some reports call Trump and Folkman board observers). Executive management did not come from WLF: CEO Peter Tassiopoulos (suspended Oct 2025), then acting CEO Jonathan Hugh, then Tony Isaac. 'Controlled at board level by WLF insiders' is accurate. 'Run by the same people' overstates it.

sub_claims.statement: ALT5 Sigma stock fell about 94% in one year.
sub_claims.finding: Outlets report declines of 90-96% depending on start and end dates. Protos measures from $8.97 before the deal to $0.35 (about 96%). Bloomberg Law (July 30, 2026) calls it a '90% rout', and TipRanks shows about 92%. About 94% is within that range.

sub_claims.statement: ALT5 rebranded from crypto to AI and is now AI Financial Corporation.
sub_claims.finding: The name changed on April 28, 2026, through a short-form merger, and the stock began trading as Nasdaq: AIFC on April 29, 2026. The company's own filing says it does not currently offer AI-enabled financial services. It is still a WLFI treasury and payments company, and in May 2026 it posted a $271M quarterly loss with a going-concern warning (a warning it later said had been mitigated).

sub_claims.statement: The SEC, whose leadership the president appoints, is the regulator that would have to act, implying it won't.
sub_claims.finding: This is commentary, not a checkable fact. POGO reports the SEC has not opened a probe despite a shareholder suit (in Nevada state court) alleging 'illegality' and 'unjust enrichment'. Gizmodo reports that suit was later withdrawn with prejudice. Former regulators quoted by the WSJ said the deal likely complies with securities law if it is fully disclosed. No evidence of political interference by the SEC was found.

corrections: The transcript says 'when World Liberty went to the stock markets'. In fact ALT5 Sigma, an already-listed Nasdaq company, raised up to $1.5B, with WLF as lead investor contributing about $750M in WLFI tokens. The other roughly $750M was cash from outside investors.

The transcript says ALT5 is 'run by the same people who run World Liberty Financial'. WLF insiders sit on ALT5's board (Zach Witkoff is chairman; Eric Trump and Zak Folkman are director or observer), but its CEOs (Tassiopoulos, Hugh, Tony Isaac) were not WLF executives.
The $500M (Trump) and $90M (Witkoff) figures are journalists' estimates of entitlements from token-sale proceeds (DT Marks DEFI gets 75%), not documented payments.
The stock decline is reported as 90-96% depending on dates; about 94% is consistent with that.
denials_and_context: A Trump Organization spokesperson said Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. have no involvement in ALT5 and no visibility into the company, as quoted in coverage of the CNBC/Bloomberg reporting.
The White House denies conflicts of interest. It says the president's assets are in a trust managed by his children and that the companies operate independently.
WLF rejects allegations of improper conduct and says it followed the required regulatory procedures.
Former regulators quoted by the WSJ said the insider deal would once have drawn scrutiny but likely complies with securities law if fully disclosed.
In Aug 2025 ALT5 denied reports that the SEC was probing investor Jon Isaac. The Nevada shareholder suit was reportedly withdrawn with prejudice.

The company had a separate governance crisis: the CEO was suspended in Oct 2025, the acting CEO and COO were removed in Nov 2025, and a Rwandan court case involved a company principal. These events are independent of the Trump-family payments.
